title: They told me to move faster.
paragraphs: They told me to move faster.
And that waiting exposed things in me I never would have seen at full speed.

Isaiah 40:31 says, “But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength…”
Not race ahead.
Not force the door.
Not panic their way into a breakthrough.
That was the lesson I learned.

Waiting revealed where I had made an idol out of control. It showed me how often I called my anxiety “wisdom” and my rushing “faith.” But real faith does not always sprint. Sometimes real faith sits still with trembling hands and says, “Lord, I still trust You.”

Waiting is not punishment for the believer.
It is often preparation.

God does deep work in delays. He breaks pride there. He purifies motives there. He teaches dependence there. The waiting room of God can feel silent, but heaven is never inactive. While you are crying over what has not happened yet, the Lord may be strengthening the very soul that will need to carry the answer when it comes.
Isaiah did not say those who wait lose their strength forever. He said they renew it. That means what felt drained can be restored. What felt weak can rise again. What felt stuck can still soar.
But that promise is not just about getting what you want. It is about getting more of God.
And the fullest proof of that is Jesus.

Humanity waited in darkness for a Savior. Centuries of longing. Centuries of prophecy. Then in the fullness of time, Christ came. He lived sinlessly, died for our sins, and rose again so that all who repent and trust in Him would not be crushed by shame, but carried by grace. The greatest waiting story in history ended in the greatest rescue.

So if you are in a season of delay, do not waste it.
Let it drive you to Christ.
Let it strip your self-reliance.
Let it teach you to hope with holy patience.
Because those who wait on the Lord do not wait in vain.

They rise.
They run.
They endure.
And in Jesus, so will you.
